last_result.content:
## 4 Retention and Deletion

The vendor must delete or return all employee data within 60 days after expiration or
termination and must certify the deletion in writing. Backup and archival copies must be
covered, with a defined purge cycle if immediate deletion is impracticable. Retention beyond
the 60-day window is acceptable only under a specific legal hold or an identified legal
requirement, only for the period that requirement runs, and only under the continuing
security and confidentiality obligations of the agreement. Open-ended retention for
unspecified legal purposes, or retention governed solely by the vendor's own schedule, is
not acceptable.

last_result.content:
## 4.1 Retention and Post-Termination Handling

Provider will retain Employee Data during the Subscription Term and thereafter for so long as
Provider determines retention is necessary or appropriate for legal, regulatory, audit, or
dispute-resolution purposes. Following expiration or termination, Provider will make Employee
Data available for Customer export for thirty (30) days, after which Provider will delete
Employee Data in accordance with Provider's standard retention schedule then in effect.
Provider has no obligation to certify deletion or to delete Employee Data held in backup,
archival, log, or aggregated form.

action.title: Inconsistent Data Retention Policy
action.analysis: The Playbook mandates that all employee data must be deleted or returned within 60 days after expiration or termination, with backup and archival copies covered under a defined purge cycle if immediate deletion is impractical. However, the Data Handling Exhibit allows for indefinite retention of data based on Provider's discretion for unspecified legal, regulatory, audit, or dispute-resolution purposes, and does not require certification of deletion or deletion of data held in backup, archival, log, or aggregated form.
action.recommendation: The Data Handling Exhibit should align with the Playbook's strict requirements for data retention and deletion.

quotes.text: The vendor must delete or return all employee data within 60 days after expiration or termination and must certify the deletion in writing. Backup and archival copies must be covered, with a defined purge cycle if immediate deletion is impractical.

Provider will retain Employee Data during the Subscription Term and thereafter for so long as Provider determines retention is necessary or appropriate for legal, regulatory, audit, or dispute-resolution purposes. Following expiration or termination, Provider will make Employee Data available for Customer export for thirty (30) days, after which Provider will delete Employee Data in accordance with Provider's standard retention schedule then in effect. Provider has no obligation to certify deletion or to delete Employee Data held in backup, archival, log, or aggregated form.

action.replacement_text: Provider will retain Employee Data during the Subscription Term and thereafter for sixty (60) days following expiration or termination, after which Provider will delete Employee Data in accordance with the following process: (i) Provider will certify in writing that all Employee Data has been deleted or returned to Customer; (ii) Provider will ensure that all backup, archival, log, and aggregated forms of Employee Data are also deleted or returned to Customer within ninety (90) days following expiration or termination; and (iii) Provider will not retain Employee Data for any longer than necessary for legal, regulatory, audit, or dispute-resolution purposes, and will provide written notice to Customer prior to retaining Employee Data beyond the sixty (60) day period.
action.rationale: This proposed redline aligns the Data Handling Exhibit with the strict requirements outlined in the Playbook for data retention and deletion, ensuring that all employee data is deleted or returned within 60 days after expiration or termination, with backup and archival copies covered under a defined purge cycle if immediate deletion is impractical.
